01.event: After twelve years in the study hall he returned home, but first sat in the local study hall and sent word ahead, so as not to repeat ben Ḥakhinai's sudden arrival.
01.turn: His unrecognized son Rabbi Oshaya came and questioned him, and Ḥama saw his sharp learning and lamented not having raised such a son.
01.outcome: He went home, his son followed, and he stood up before him; his wife scolded that a father does not rise for a son, and Rami bar Ḥama applied the verse about a threefold cord to Oshaya.
01.summary: Rabbi Ḥama bar Bisa spent twelve years studying away. On returning he resolved not to surprise his wife as ben Ḥakhinai had, so he waited in the study hall and sent word ahead. There a young man he did not recognize questioned him sharply, and Ḥama regretted missing his own son's upbringing. At home he rose before the youth, his wife pointed out he was standing for his own son, and the verse of the threefold cord was applied to the family.

02.event: Visiting Benei Berak, he saw goats grazing under fig trees with honey dripping from the figs and milk from the goats, mixing together.
02.turn: He recognized it as the meaning of the verse 'a land flowing with milk and honey'.
02.summary: Rami bar Yeḥezkel visited Benei Berak and saw goats grazing under fig trees. Honey oozed from the figs and milk dripped from the goats, and the two mixed together. He remarked that this is what 'flowing with milk and honey' means.
02.missing: This is a brief anecdote of observation with no real conflict or resolution.

03.actor: A woman obliged to take an oath, and Rav Beivai bar Abaye
03.event: A woman required to swear in Rav Beivai's court was asked by her opponent to swear in her own town; she demanded a document of rights first, and Rav Beivai ordered it written.
03.turn: Rav Pappi rebuked Rav Beivai, playing on his family's unfortunate lineage, for ordering the document written.
03.outcome: No resolution of the incident is given; only Rav Pappi's rebuke and the legal reasoning behind it follow.
03.summary: A woman owed an oath in Rav Beivai bar Abaye's court. Her opponent wanted her to swear in town, hoping shame would make her confess. She insisted on first receiving a document of rights, and Rav Beivai told the court to write it. Rav Pappi then rebuked him with a pun on his unlucky family.
03.missing: How the incident actually ended; the explanation of Rav Pappi's objection is in later segments.

04.actor: A man who betrothed with a myrtle branch; Rav Aḥa bar Huna and Rav Yosef
04.event: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace, and Rav Aḥa bar Huna sent the question to Rav Yosef.
04.turn: Rav Yosef answered with a compromise ruling.
04.outcome: Rav Yosef ruled that the man be flogged (per Rav) and the woman require a bill of divorce (per Shmuel).
04.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace. Rav Aḥa bar Huna asked Rav Yosef what to do. Rav Yosef replied that the man should be flogged and that she should still receive a divorce document, just in case the branch was worth a peruta somewhere.

06.actor: Rav Yosef and his student Abaye
06.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a certain ruling, and Abaye reminded him that he himself had taught it, citing the mishna and Rav Yehuda's statement.
06.turn: Rav Yosef's memory was lost through illness, and his student corrected him.
06.summary: Rav Yosef said he had not heard a certain ruling. Abaye replied that Rav Yosef himself had taught it to them, and quoted the mishna and Rav Yehuda's explanation. Rav Yosef's response is not given.
06.missing: Rav Yosef's reaction; the exchange is mostly a legal citation.

07.event: A man did each of them a small favor (removing a feather from Ameimar's head; covering spittle before Mar Ukva) and then revealed he had a case before them.
07.turn: Each realized the favor created a bond that compromised impartiality.
07.outcome: Each judge disqualified himself from hearing the man's case.
07.summary: While Ameimar was judging, a feather landed on his head and a man removed it. When the man said he had a case before him, Ameimar disqualified himself because of the favor. Likewise a man covered spittle lying before Mar Ukva, and Mar Ukva disqualified himself from his case too.

08.event: Ulla, who used to go up to Eretz Yisrael, died outside the land, and Rabbi Elazar was told.
08.turn: Rabbi Elazar lamented that the verse about dying in an unclean land was fulfilled; told that Ulla's coffin was being brought to Eretz Yisrael, he said it is not the same as being absorbed in its soil while alive.
08.outcome: Rabbi Elazar maintained that burial there after death does not equal living there.
08.summary: Ulla often went up to Eretz Yisrael but died abroad. When Rabbi Elazar heard, he mourned that Ulla had died in an unclean land. Told that the coffin was being brought to Eretz Yisrael, he replied that being absorbed by its soil in life is not like being absorbed after death.

10.actor: A man in Jerusalem with much movable property
10.event: Wanting to give away his movable property as a gift, he was advised the only way was through land, so he acquired a small plot and declared it given to someone together with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels.
10.turn: He died, and the question arose whether the gift took effect.
10.outcome: The Sages fulfilled his statement and gave the gifts.
10.summary: A man in Jerusalem, perhaps ill, wanted to give away a large amount of movable property. Told he could only do so by means of land, he bought a tiny plot and declared it, along with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, given to a certain person. He died, and the Sages carried out his declaration.

11.actor: A woman visiting her husband's grave, and a guard
11.event: She had intercourse with a man guarding the body of someone executed by the king; when that body was taken, she suggested they exhume her husband so the guard could claim he had done his job.
11.turn: The body was stolen and the pair used her husband's corpse as a substitute.
11.outcome: She had her husband removed from his grave; the incident is cited to show sin is possible even in acute mourning.
11.summary: A woman went to her husband's grave and there had intercourse with a man guarding a body hung by the king. The body was taken, so she proposed digging up her husband's corpse for the guard to present instead. It is told as proof that even mourners can succumb to temptation.
11.missing: The incident is only briefly summarized in a commentary's terms.

12.event: Avimi, though ordained and father of five ordained sons, ran to open the door whenever his father called, answering 'yes, yes' before arriving; one day his father asked for water and fell asleep before he returned.
12.turn: Avimi did not wake or leave his father but stood bent over him until he awoke.
12.outcome: His devotion was rewarded: he was helped in his learning and succeeded in interpreting the psalm 'A song to Asaph'.
12.summary: Avimi honored his father Rabbi Abbahu so carefully that even as a distinguished sage he hurried to open the door and called out in advance. Once his father asked for water and dozed off before it arrived, so Avimi stood over him until he woke. As a reward his learning was aided and he could interpret a psalm.

13.event: Rabbi Akiva ridiculed transgressors; Satan appeared to him as a woman at the top of a palm tree and he climbed after her.
13.turn: Halfway up, the evil inclination left him and said it would have destroyed him if not for heaven's proclamation protecting him.
13.outcome: Akiva was spared only because of his standing in heaven.
13.summary: Rabbi Akiva used to mock those who sinned. One day Satan appeared to him as a woman at the top of a palm tree, and he grabbed the trunk and began climbing. Halfway up the evil inclination left him and said that only the heavenly warning to be careful with Akiva and his Torah saved him from being ruined.
